question: According to the legislative findings in Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2401, why did the Nebraska Legislature codify real estate brokerage relationships in statute?
choice_a: Because federal law required states to adopt uniform agency statutes
choice_b: Because the Nebraska Supreme Court struck down common-law agency as void for vagueness
choice_c: Because applying the common law of agency to broker-client relationships had produced misunderstandings and outcomes contrary to the public interest, and because the real estate industry has a significant impact on Nebraska's economy
choice_d: Because the National Association of Realtors petitioned for codification
explanation: Section 76-2401 states the Legislature found that applying common-law agency to real estate relationships caused misunderstandings contrary to the public interest, that the brokerage industry significantly impacts Nebraska's economy, and that it is in the public interest to codify these relationships in statute.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2403, an 'adverse material fact' includes a fact that significantly affects the desirability or value of the property to a party and:
choice_a: Was disclosed in a prior transaction
choice_b: Is listed on the property's tax record
choice_c: Relates only to the buyer's personal taste
choice_d: Is not reasonably ascertainable or known to that party
explanation: Section 76-2403(1) defines an adverse material fact as one that significantly affects the desirability or value of the property to a party and is not reasonably ascertainable or known to that party.

question: Besides facts affecting a property's desirability or value, §76-2403 also defines 'adverse material fact' to include a fact establishing:
choice_a: A reasonable belief that another party will not be able to, or does not intend to, complete that party's obligations under a contract creating an interest in real property
choice_b: That a licensee's commission is negotiable
choice_c: That a property was previously listed by a competing brokerage
choice_d: That the buyer has pre-qualified for financing
explanation: The second prong of §76-2403(2) covers facts establishing a reasonable belief that a party will not be able to, or does not intend to, complete that party's contractual obligations regarding an interest in real property.

question: A seller's agent learns the seller has stopped making mortgage payments and likely cannot convey clear title at closing. Under §76-2403, how should this fact be classified?
choice_a: Irrelevant, because it concerns the seller's finances rather than the property itself
choice_b: An adverse material fact, because it establishes a reasonable belief the seller cannot complete the contract obligations
choice_c: Confidential information that may never be disclosed to anyone under any circumstance
choice_d: Not a concern for the agent since only attorneys handle title issues
explanation: This fits the second prong of the adverse-material-fact definition: it establishes a reasonable belief that the seller will not be able to complete the contractual obligation of conveying clear title.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2404, an 'affiliated licensee' is:
choice_a: Any person licensed anywhere in the United States
choice_b: A licensee related by blood or marriage to a designated broker
choice_c: An associate broker or salesperson (as defined in the Nebraska Real Estate License Act) who is under the supervision of a designated broker
choice_d: A part-time licensee working for two brokers at once
explanation: Section 76-2404 defines 'affiliated licensee' as an associate broker or salesperson, as defined in §81-885.01, who is under the supervision of a designated broker.

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2404.01 defines 'asset management company' as a business firm or association that sells, conveys, or offers an interest in real property belonging to, among others:
choice_a: A private homeowner selling a personal residence
choice_b: An individual real estate salesperson
choice_c: A title insurance underwriter
choice_d: A bank, savings and loan association, or other state- or federally-regulated financial institution
explanation: Section 76-2404.01 lists banks, savings and loan associations, and other state- or federally-regulated financial institutions (as well as congressionally chartered mortgage-holding entities and government entities) as the entities whose property an asset management company may sell or convey.

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2405 defines 'brokerage relationship' as the relationship created between a client and:
choice_a: A designated broker, and, by extension, that broker's affiliated licensees
choice_b: The State Real Estate Commission
choice_c: Any Nebraska licensee, regardless of employment
choice_d: The escrow or title company handling the closing
explanation: Section 76-2405 defines 'brokerage relationship' as the relationship between a designated broker and a client, which also extends to the relationship created between the client and the designated broker's affiliated licensees.

question: Under §76-2406, 'confidential information' means information made confidential by:
choice_a: Any conversation overheard by a licensee at an open house
choice_b: Statute, rule, regulation, or written instructions from the client
choice_c: The rules of the local multiple listing service alone
choice_d: Verbal requests from an unrepresented customer
explanation: Section 76-2406 defines confidential information as information made confidential by statute, rule, regulation, or written instructions from the client, unless it becomes public.

question: Under §76-2406, information a client instructed be kept confidential loses that protected status once it:
choice_a: Is more than 30 days old
choice_b: Is shared with the client's accountant
choice_c: Is made public, or becomes public through the words or conduct of the client, or comes from a source other than the licensee
choice_d: Is committed to writing
explanation: Section 76-2406 excludes from 'confidential information' anything that becomes public through the client's own words or conduct, or that originates from a source other than the licensee.

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2407 defines 'client' as:
choice_a: Any person who calls a real estate office to ask about a listing
choice_b: A person who has only a non-binding oral understanding with a licensee
choice_c: The licensee's own employing broker
choice_d: A seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant who has entered into a brokerage relationship with a licensee and to whom the licensee owes the statutory duties
explanation: Section 76-2407 defines 'client' as a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant who has entered into a brokerage relationship with a licensee under §§76-2401 to 76-2430 and to whom the licensee owes the statutory duty.

question: The core statutory distinction between a 'client' (§76-2407) and a 'customer' (§76-2409) is that:
choice_a: A client has entered into a brokerage relationship with the licensee, while a customer has not
choice_b: A client always pays a commission and a customer never does
choice_c: A client is always the buyer and a customer is always the seller
choice_d: There is no legal distinction between the two terms
explanation: A 'client' has entered into a brokerage relationship and is owed the full statutory duties under §§76-2417 to 76-2419; a 'customer' has not entered into such a relationship and is owed only limited duties, chiefly adverse-material-fact disclosure.

question: Under §76-2409, a 'customer' is defined as:
choice_a: A party who has signed a written buyer agency agreement
choice_b: A seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant in a transaction involving a licensee who has NOT entered into a brokerage relationship with that licensee
choice_c: Any person who attends an open house
choice_d: The licensee's employing designated broker
explanation: Section 76-2409 defines 'customer' as a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant in a real estate transaction in which a licensee is involved but who has not entered into a brokerage relationship with that licensee.

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2410 defines 'designated broker' by cross-reference to which statute?
choice_a: Section 76-2417
choice_b: Section 81-885.24
choice_c: Section 81-885.01 of the Nebraska Real Estate License Act
choice_d: The Nebraska Uniform Commercial Code
explanation: Section 76-2410 provides that 'designated broker' has the same meaning as in §81-885.01 of the Nebraska Real Estate License Act.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2411, a 'dual agent' is a limited agent who represents both the seller and buyer (or landlord and tenant) in a transaction:
choice_a: Automatically, whenever the same brokerage lists and sells the property
choice_b: Only with the commission's prior written approval
choice_c: Without needing any party's consent, so long as compensation is disclosed
choice_d: With the written informed consent of all parties to the contemplated transaction
explanation: Section 76-2411 defines a dual agent as a limited agent who, with the written informed consent of all parties to a contemplated transaction, represents both the seller and buyer or both the landlord and tenant.

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2412 defines 'licensee' to include which three categories (each as defined in §81-885.01)?
choice_a: A designated broker, an associate broker, and a salesperson
choice_b: A buyer, a seller, and a title agent
choice_c: A landlord, a tenant, and a property manager
choice_d: The commission, the director, and the Attorney General
explanation: Section 76-2412 defines 'licensee' as a designated broker, an associate broker, and a salesperson, all as defined in §81-885.01.

question: Under §76-2413, a 'limited agent' is a licensee whose duties and obligations to a client are set forth in which sections?
choice_a: Sections 81-885.11 through 81-885.24
choice_b: Sections 76-2417 through 76-2419
choice_c: Sections 76-2401 and 76-2402 only
choice_d: The unmodified common law of agency
explanation: Section 76-2413 defines 'limited agent' as a licensee whose duties and obligations to a client are those set forth in §§76-2417 to 76-2419.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2414, a 'single agent' who represents only one party may be a buyer's agent, a seller's agent, a landlord's agent, or:
choice_a: A dual agent
choice_b: A subagent for the opposing party
choice_c: A tenant's agent
choice_d: A designated broker acting for the commission
explanation: Section 76-2414 lists the four types of single agent: buyer's agent, landlord's agent, seller's agent, and tenant's agent.

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2415 defines a 'subagent' as:
choice_a: A licensee who works exclusively for the State Real Estate Commission
choice_b: A salesperson who has not yet obtained a broker's license
choice_c: A licensee representing both parties without disclosure
choice_d: A designated broker, together with his or her affiliated licensees, engaged by another designated broker to act as a limited agent for a client
explanation: Section 76-2415 defines a subagent as a designated broker, together with his or her affiliated licensees, engaged by another designated broker to act as a limited agent for a client.

question: Under §76-2415, a subagent owes the client the same obligations under §§76-2417 and 76-2418 as:
choice_a: The client's primary designated broker
choice_b: The opposing party's agent
choice_c: The State Real Estate Commission
choice_d: No one — a subagent owes no duties to the client
explanation: Section 76-2415 provides that a subagent owes the same obligations and responsibilities to the client as does the client's primary designated broker.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2416(2), absent one of the statutory exceptions, a licensee is presumed by default to be:
choice_a: The seller's or landlord's limited agent
choice_b: The buyer's or tenant's limited agent
choice_c: A dual agent for both parties
choice_d: A subagent of the listing broker
explanation: Section 76-2416(2) establishes that a licensee shall be considered a buyer's or tenant's limited agent unless one of four listed exceptions applies (a written seller's/landlord's agreement, a subagency agreement, a written dual agency agreement, or another written agency agreement). This statutory default is a key and frequently tested feature of Nebraska agency law.

question: Under §76-2416(2)(a), the default buyer's/tenant's agent presumption is overcome when the designated broker instead:
choice_a: Simply tells the buyer verbally that the broker represents the seller
choice_b: Posts a 'for sale' sign including the seller's name
choice_c: Enters into a written seller's agent or landlord's agent agreement with the party to be represented, per §76-2422(2)
choice_d: Accepts a referral fee from another brokerage
explanation: Section 76-2416(2)(a) overcomes the default buyer's/tenant's agency presumption when the designated broker enters into a written seller's agent or landlord's agent agreement under §76-2422(2).

question: Under §76-2416(2)(c), the default buyer's/tenant's agent presumption is overcome when the designated broker enters into:
choice_a: An oral dual agency understanding
choice_b: A verbal listing agreement
choice_c: A referral agreement with an unlicensed party
choice_d: A written dual agency agreement with the parties to be represented, per §76-2422(4)
explanation: Section 76-2416(2)(c) overcomes the default presumption when the designated broker enters into a written dual agency agreement under §76-2422(4).

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2416(3), sections 76-2401 to 76-2430 do not obligate a buyer or tenant to pay compensation to a licensee unless:
choice_a: The buyer or tenant has entered into a written agreement with the designated broker specifying the compensation terms
choice_b: The buyer verbally promises to pay a commission
choice_c: The buyer has viewed at least three properties with the licensee
choice_d: A court orders the buyer to pay compensation
explanation: Section 76-2416(3) states that no buyer or tenant is obligated to pay compensation to a licensee absent a written agreement specifying compensation terms, consistent with §76-2422(3).

question: Under §76-2416(4), which arrangement is expressly permitted?
choice_a: Representing the same client as a dual agent in two separate transactions without any consent
choice_b: Selling one property for a person as a seller's agent, then helping that same person buy a different property as a buyer's agent, provided each relationship is properly established
choice_c: Never working with the same client twice
choice_d: Requiring commission pre-approval for each repeat transaction with the same client
explanation: Section 76-2416(4) allows a licensee to work with a single party in separate transactions under different relationships, such as selling one property as a seller's agent and helping that same seller buy another property as a buyer's agent, as long as each relationship complies with the statute.

question: Under §76-2416(1), when engaged in licensed brokerage activities, a licensee may act as a limited agent in a transaction as:
choice_a: Only a single agent — Nebraska law prohibits subagency and dual agency
choice_b: Only a dual agent
choice_c: A single agent, a subagent, or a dual agent
choice_d: A trustee, executor, or guardian
explanation: Section 76-2416(1) authorizes a licensee to act as a limited agent in any transaction as a single agent, subagent, or dual agent (or alternatively as an agent under a written contract per §76-2422(6)).

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2417(1)(a), a seller's or landlord's agent's first enumerated duty is to:
choice_a: Guarantee the sale will close within 30 days
choice_b: Personally inspect the property for latent defects
choice_c: Refuse all offers below the listing price
choice_d: Perform the terms of the written agreement made with the client
explanation: Section 76-2417(1)(a) requires a seller's or landlord's agent to perform the terms of the written agreement made with the client.

question: Section 76-2417(1)(b) requires a seller's or landlord's agent to:
choice_a: Exercise reasonable skill and care for the client
choice_b: Exercise the highest skill obtainable in the industry regardless of cost
choice_c: Delegate all skill-based tasks to a supervising broker
choice_d: Warrant the accuracy of statements made by third-party inspectors
explanation: Section 76-2417(1)(b) requires the seller's or landlord's agent to exercise reasonable skill and care for the client.

question: Under §76-2417(1)(c)(i), a seller's agent must seek a price and terms acceptable to the client but is NOT obligated to:
choice_a: Disclose the listing price to prospective buyers
choice_b: Seek additional offers to purchase while the property is already subject to a contract for sale (or additional offers to lease while under a lease or letter of intent)
choice_c: Communicate with the seller once a contract is signed
choice_d: Return earnest money deposits to a buyer
explanation: Section 76-2417(1)(c)(i) carves out that the licensee need not seek additional purchase offers once the property is under contract for sale, or additional lease offers once subject to a lease or letter of intent to lease.

question: Under §76-2417(1)(c)(ii), a seller's or landlord's agent must present all written offers to and from the client in a timely manner:
choice_a: Only if the offer meets or exceeds the listing price
choice_b: Only during the first 10 days the property is listed
choice_c: Regardless of whether the property is already subject to a contract for sale or lease or a letter of intent to lease (subject to the §76-2422.01 exception for asset management company clients)
choice_d: Only if the offering party is represented by a licensee
explanation: Section 76-2417(1)(c)(ii) requires timely presentation of all written offers regardless of existing contract status, except as exempted under §76-2422.01 for asset management company clients.

question: Under §76-2417(1)(c)(iii), a seller's or landlord's agent must disclose to the client, in writing:
choice_a: Only adverse material facts the client already suspects
choice_b: Only facts disclosed to the licensee by the buyer
choice_c: Nothing, since the client already owns the property
choice_d: All adverse material facts actually known by the licensee
explanation: Section 76-2417(1)(c)(iii) requires written disclosure to the client of all adverse material facts actually known by the licensee.

question: Section 76-2417(1)(c)(iv) requires a seller's or landlord's agent to advise the client to obtain expert advice regarding:
choice_a: Material matters the licensee knows about but the specifics of which are beyond the licensee's own expertise
choice_b: Any matter whatsoever, even matters clearly within the licensee's own expertise
choice_c: Only tax matters
choice_d: Only zoning matters
explanation: Section 76-2417(1)(c)(iv) requires the agent to advise the client to seek expert advice on material matters known to the licensee but whose specifics exceed the licensee's expertise.

question: Under §76-2417(1)(d), a seller's or landlord's agent must:
choice_a: Deposit all earnest money into the licensee's personal operating account
choice_b: Account in a timely manner for all money and property received
choice_c: Wait until closing to account for any funds received
choice_d: Provide an accounting only if the client demands one in writing
explanation: Section 76-2417(1)(d) requires the agent to account in a timely manner for all money and property received.

question: Under §76-2417(3)(a), a licensee acting as a seller's or landlord's agent owes no duty or obligation to a buyer or prospective buyer, except the duty to:
choice_a: Negotiate the lowest possible price on the buyer's behalf
choice_b: Recommend a home inspector to the buyer
choice_c: Disclose in writing all adverse material facts actually known by the licensee
choice_d: Represent the buyer's interests equally alongside the seller's
explanation: Section 76-2417(3)(a) provides that a seller's or landlord's agent owes no duty to a buyer except to disclose in writing all adverse material facts actually known by the licensee.

question: Under §76-2417(3)(b), a seller's or landlord's agent owes no duty to:
choice_a: Disclose the listing agreement's expiration date to the seller
choice_b: Present offers to the seller
choice_c: Comply with fair housing laws
choice_d: Conduct an independent inspection of the property for the buyer's benefit, or independently verify statements made by the client or any independent inspector
explanation: Section 76-2417(3)(b) states the seller's/landlord's agent owes no duty to independently inspect the property for the buyer's benefit or independently verify the client's or an inspector's statements.

question: Under §76-2417(4), a seller's or landlord's agent may, without breaching any duty to the client:
choice_a: Show alternative properties not owned by the client to prospective buyers and list competing properties for sale or lease
choice_b: Never show any other property to a prospective buyer
choice_c: Only show properties owned by relatives of the client
choice_d: Disclose the seller's confidential bottom-line price to a competing buyer
explanation: Section 76-2417(4) permits a seller's or landlord's agent to show alternative properties and list competing properties without breaching any duty to the client.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2418(1)(a), a buyer's or tenant's agent's duty is to:
choice_a: Guarantee the lowest possible purchase price
choice_b: Perform the terms of any written agreement made with the client
choice_c: Refuse to show any property listed by the agent's own brokerage
choice_d: Personally finance the client's earnest money deposit
explanation: Section 76-2418(1)(a) requires the buyer's or tenant's agent to perform the terms of any written agreement made with the client.

question: Under §76-2418(1)(c)(i), a buyer's or tenant's agent must seek a price and terms acceptable to the client but is NOT obligated to:
choice_a: Ever show the client more than one property
choice_b: Disclose the buyer's identity to the seller
choice_c: Seek other properties while the client is already a party to a contract to purchase, or to a lease or letter of intent to lease
choice_d: Negotiate on the client's behalf at all
explanation: Section 76-2418(1)(c)(i) mirrors the seller's-agent exception: the buyer's/tenant's agent need not seek other properties once the client is already under contract or a lease/letter of intent.

question: Under §76-2418(3)(a), a buyer's or tenant's agent owes no duty to a seller or prospective seller except the duty to disclose in writing all adverse material facts actually known, which may include:
choice_a: The buyer's confidential maximum offer price
choice_b: The buyer's motivations for wanting the property
choice_c: The buyer's other pending offers on competing properties
choice_d: Adverse material facts concerning the client's financial ability to perform the terms of the transaction
explanation: Section 76-2418(3)(a) gives the client's financial ability to perform the transaction as an example of an adverse material fact a buyer's/tenant's agent must disclose to the seller.

question: Under §76-2418(3)(b), a buyer's or tenant's agent owes no duty to:
choice_a: Conduct an independent investigation of the client's financial condition for the customer's benefit, or independently verify statements made by the client or an inspector
choice_b: Present any offers to the seller
choice_c: Disclose known adverse material facts about the property's condition
choice_d: Comply with the Nebraska Real Estate License Act
explanation: Section 76-2418(3)(b) relieves a buyer's/tenant's agent of any duty to independently investigate the client's finances for the customer's benefit or verify statements made by the client or an inspector.

question: Under §76-2418(4), a buyer's or tenant's agent may, without breaching any duty to the client:
choice_a: Never show a property to more than one prospective buyer
choice_b: Show properties the client is interested in to other prospective buyers or tenants, including showing competing buyers the same property
choice_c: Disclose the client's confidential maximum offer to a competing buyer
choice_d: Represent the seller in the same transaction without consent
explanation: Section 76-2418(4) allows a buyer's/tenant's agent to show the same property to competing prospective buyers or tenants without breaching any duty to the client.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2419(1), a licensee may act as a dual agent only:
choice_a: With the verbal consent of just the seller
choice_b: With the commission's prior written approval, regardless of the parties' wishes
choice_c: With the informed consent of all parties to the transaction, evidenced by a written agreement under §76-2422
choice_d: Automatically, once both parties are represented by licensees at the same brokerage
explanation: Section 76-2419(1) requires the informed consent of all parties, evidenced by a written agreement under §76-2422, before a licensee may act as a dual agent.

question: Under §76-2419(2), a dual agent is a limited agent for both parties and has the duties required by:
choice_a: The unmodified common law of agency only
choice_b: Section 76-2409 (the customer definition) only
choice_c: No statutory duties; dual agents are exempt from all duties
choice_d: Sections 76-2417 and 76-2418, except as otherwise provided in §76-2419
explanation: Section 76-2419(2) provides that a dual agent has the duties and obligations required of a seller's/landlord's agent and buyer's/tenant's agent under §§76-2417 and 76-2418, except as modified within §76-2419 itself.

question: Under §76-2419(4)(a), a dual agent may NOT disclose, without the informed written consent of the affected client, that:
choice_a: A buyer or tenant is willing to pay more than the purchase price or lease rate offered for the property
choice_b: The seller has accepted an offer
choice_c: The property has adverse material facts
choice_d: The closing date has been agreed upon
explanation: Section 76-2419(4)(a) bars a dual agent from disclosing, absent informed written consent, that a buyer or tenant is willing to pay more than the price or rate offered.

question: Under §76-2419(4)(b), which information may a dual agent NOT disclose without the affected client's informed written consent?
choice_a: The property's square footage
choice_b: That a seller or landlord is willing to accept less than the asking price or lease rate for the property
choice_c: The property's zoning classification
choice_d: The name of the title company handling closing
explanation: Section 76-2419(4)(b) prohibits a dual agent from disclosing, without informed written consent, that a seller or landlord will accept less than the asking price or lease rate.

question: Under §76-2419(4)(c), a dual agent is barred, absent informed written consent, from disclosing:
choice_a: The property's legal description
choice_b: The date the property was originally listed
choice_c: What the motivating factors are for any client buying, selling, or leasing the property
choice_d: Whether the property has a homeowners association
explanation: Section 76-2419(4)(c) protects a client's motivating factors for the transaction from disclosure by a dual agent without informed written consent.

question: Under §76-2419(4)(d), a dual agent may not disclose without informed written consent that:
choice_a: The property is subject to a recorded easement
choice_b: The buyer intends to use the property as a rental
choice_c: The seller previously reduced the asking price
choice_d: A client will agree to financing terms other than those offered
explanation: Section 76-2419(4)(d) bars disclosure, absent informed written consent, that a client will agree to financing terms other than those offered.

question: Under §76-2419(3), despite restrictions on sensitive disclosures, a dual agent must still:
choice_a: Disclose to both clients all adverse material facts actually known by the licensee
choice_b: Keep all adverse material facts confidential from both clients
choice_c: Disclose adverse material facts only to the party paying the commission
choice_d: Report adverse material facts only to the commission
explanation: Section 76-2419(3) requires a dual agent to disclose all actually known adverse material facts to both clients, even though certain other sensitive information is restricted under subsection (4).

question: Under §76-2419(5)(b)-(c), when a dual agent makes a disclosure that is required or permitted by statute, that disclosure:
choice_a: Automatically terminates the dual-agency relationship
choice_b: Does not give rise to a cause of action against the dual agent and does not terminate the dual-agency relationship
choice_c: Exposes the dual agent to civil liability regardless of the circumstances
choice_d: Requires prior commission approval
explanation: Section 76-2419(5)(b) and (c) provide immunity from suit for required or permitted disclosures and clarify that making such a disclosure does not terminate the dual-agency relationship.

question: Under §76-2419(6), in a dual-agency relationship, there shall be:
choice_a: Full imputation of all knowledge between both clients automatically
choice_b: Imputation of knowledge only regarding financing terms
choice_c: No imputation of knowledge or information between any client and the dual agent, or among persons within an entity engaged as a dual agent
choice_d: Imputation of knowledge only if the dual agent is a designated broker
explanation: Section 76-2419(6) eliminates imputation of knowledge or information between clients and the dual agent, and among persons within an entity acting as dual agent.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2420(1), every designated broker must adopt:
choice_a: A verbal policy communicated only to new hires
choice_b: A policy approved individually by the Attorney General
choice_c: No policy at all — policies are optional under the statute
choice_d: A written policy identifying and describing the relationships in which the designated broker and affiliated licensees may engage with sellers, landlords, buyers, or tenants
explanation: Section 76-2420(1) requires every designated broker to adopt a written policy identifying and describing the brokerage relationships the broker and affiliated licensees may engage in.

question: Under §76-2420(2), a designated broker:
choice_a: Is not required to offer or engage in more than one of the brokerage relationships enumerated in §76-2416
choice_b: Must offer all four types of brokerage relationships to every client
choice_c: Must obtain commission approval before choosing which relationships to offer
choice_d: May only offer dual agency
explanation: Section 76-2420(2) clarifies that a designated broker need not offer or engage in more than one of the brokerage relationships listed in §76-2416.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2421(1), a licensee offering brokerage services must make the required disclosures:
choice_a: Only at closing
choice_b: At the earliest practicable opportunity during or following the first substantial contact with a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant who has not entered into a written brokerage agreement
choice_c: Within 24 hours after a written offer is accepted
choice_d: Only if the customer specifically requests it in writing
explanation: Section 76-2421(1) sets the disclosure timing as the earliest practicable opportunity during or following first substantial contact with an unrepresented party.

question: Under §76-2421(1)(a), the required initial disclosure includes providing the person with:
choice_a: A copy of the licensee's personal résumé
choice_b: A copy of the entire Nebraska Real Estate License Act
choice_c: A written copy of the current brokerage disclosure pamphlet prepared and approved by the commission
choice_d: A copy of the property's title insurance policy
explanation: Section 76-2421(1)(a) requires providing a written copy of the current brokerage disclosure pamphlet prepared and approved by the State Real Estate Commission.

question: Under §76-2421(1)(b), in addition to the pamphlet, the licensee must disclose in writing:
choice_a: The licensee's personal commission split with the designated broker
choice_b: The licensee's years of experience
choice_c: The property's assessed tax value
choice_d: The types of brokerage relationships being offered, or which party the licensee is representing
explanation: Section 76-2421(1)(b) requires written disclosure of the types of brokerage relationships offered, or which party the licensee represents.

question: Under §76-2421(3), before engaging in licensed activities with an unrepresented buyer or tenant, a licensee working for the seller or landlord must provide a written disclosure stating that the licensee:
choice_a: Is an agent for the seller or landlord and is not an agent for the customer, along with a list of tasks the agent may perform with the customer
choice_b: Represents both parties equally as a dual agent
choice_c: Owes the customer the full fiduciary duties identical to those owed a client
choice_d: Will not disclose any information to the seller
explanation: Section 76-2421(3) requires a written disclosure stating the licensee is the seller's/landlord's agent (not the customer's agent) and listing tasks the agent may perform with the customer.

question: Under §76-2421(5), the written disclosures required under subsections (1), (3), and (4) must contain a signature block, and if the customer refuses to sign:
choice_a: The transaction is automatically void
choice_b: The licensee shall note that fact on a copy of the disclosure and retain the copy
choice_c: The licensee must terminate the relationship immediately
choice_d: The commission must be notified within 24 hours
explanation: Section 76-2421(5) requires the licensee to note a customer's refusal to sign on a retained copy of the disclosure; it does not void the transaction or require commission notification.

question: Under §76-2421(5), a customer's signed acknowledgment of receiving the required disclosure:
choice_a: Automatically creates a binding buyer agency agreement
choice_b: Obligates the customer to pay a commission
choice_c: Does not by itself constitute a contract with the licensee
choice_d: Waives the customer's right to receive adverse material fact disclosures
explanation: Section 76-2421(5) clarifies that acknowledging receipt of the disclosure does not itself create a contract with the licensee.

question: Under §76-2421(6), a licensee is NOT required to give the written disclosures otherwise required by §76-2421 to:
choice_a: Any first-time homebuyer
choice_b: Any buyer represented by an attorney
choice_c: Any seller who is also a licensed real estate agent
choice_d: Certain corporations, LLCs, partnerships, or similarly registrable entities purchasing, leasing, or selling property with five or more residential units, or property zoned or assessed as commercial or industrial
explanation: Section 76-2421(6) exempts disclosures to certain business entities transacting in five-or-more-unit residential property or commercial/industrial-classified property.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2422(1), written agreements for brokerage services are entered into by:
choice_a: The designated broker on behalf of that broker and affiliated licensees, unless the designated broker authorizes affiliated licensees in writing to sign on the broker's behalf
choice_b: Any affiliated licensee acting entirely independently of the designated broker
choice_c: The State Real Estate Commission on behalf of the parties
choice_d: The buyer's or seller's attorney exclusively
explanation: Section 76-2422(1) requires that written brokerage agreements be entered into by the designated broker, or by an affiliated licensee the broker has authorized in writing.

question: Under §76-2422(2), a written single agency agreement with a seller or landlord must include the licensee's duties under §76-2417, the terms of compensation, a fixed date of expiration, and:
choice_a: The buyer's personal financial information
choice_b: Whether an offer of subagency may be made to any other designated broker
choice_c: The commission's approval signature
choice_d: A waiver of the seller's right to receive adverse material fact disclosures
explanation: Section 76-2422(2) requires the seller's/landlord's agency agreement to also address whether the broker may offer subagency to other designated brokers.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2422(3)(a) — reflecting Nebraska's 2025 mandatory buyer-representation-agreement amendment — before performing licensed acts, a designated broker acting as a single agent for a buyer of residential property containing one to four dwelling units:
choice_a: May, but is not required to, enter into a written agreement with the buyer
choice_b: Is prohibited from entering into any written agreement with the buyer
choice_c: Shall enter into a written agency agreement with the buyer; this is a mandatory requirement, unlike agreements for other property types under §76-2422(3)(b)
choice_d: Need only obtain a verbal agreement with the buyer
explanation: Section 76-2422(3)(a) uses mandatory 'shall' language for a single agent representing a buyer of one-to-four-unit residential property, reflecting the mandatory written buyer-agency-agreement requirement effective July 1, 2025 — distinct from the permissive 'may' language in subsection (3)(b) for other property types.

question: Under §76-2422(3)(b), for property types other than one-to-four-unit residential property, a designated broker acting as a single agent for a buyer or tenant:
choice_a: Must always enter into a written agreement identical to the mandatory residential requirement
choice_b: Is barred from ever representing the buyer
choice_c: Must obtain the seller's consent first
choice_d: May enter into a written agency agreement with the party to be represented — it is not mandatory as it is for one-to-four-unit residential property
explanation: Section 76-2422(3)(b) uses permissive 'may' language for non-residential or larger properties, in contrast to the mandatory requirement in (3)(a) for one-to-four-unit residential property.

question: Under §76-2422(4), before acting as a dual agent, a designated broker must obtain written consent that includes the licensee's duties under §76-2419, and the parties must additionally confirm in writing:
choice_a: The dual-agency status and which party or parties are responsible for paying any compensation, prior to or at the time a purchase contract, lease, or letter of intent is entered into for the specific property
choice_b: The exact commission percentage split between all brokers involved, filed with the commission
choice_c: That the buyer waives all rights under the Nebraska Real Estate License Act
choice_d: That the seller has independently verified the buyer's creditworthiness
explanation: Section 76-2422(4) requires written confirmation of dual-agency status and compensation responsibility at or before the specific transaction's contract, lease, or letter of intent is signed.

question: Under §76-2422(5), before acting as a subagent, a designated broker must:
choice_a: Obtain the commission's prior approval
choice_b: Enter into a written contract with the primary designated broker for the client (or, if the primary broker made a unilateral offer of subagency, enter the relationship by disclosing subagent status to the customer)
choice_c: Simply notify the client verbally
choice_d: Do nothing further, since subagency arises automatically from an MLS listing
explanation: Section 76-2422(5) requires a written subagency contract with the primary designated broker, or, for a unilateral offer of subagency, entry via disclosure of subagent status to the customer.

question: Under §76-2422(6), when a designated broker's agreement with a party imposes duties and responsibilities exceeding those in §§76-2417 and 76-2418, that agreement:
choice_a: Is void as a matter of law
choice_b: Automatically converts the relationship into dual agency
choice_c: Is subject to the common-law requirements of agency applicable to real estate licensees
choice_d: Cannot include any duty of confidentiality
explanation: Section 76-2422(6) provides that an agreement exceeding the statutory duties of §§76-2417/76-2418 is subject to the common-law requirements of agency applicable to real estate licensees — a notable exception to the statute's general supersession of common law under §76-2429.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2422.01, when a licensee's client is an 'asset management company,' the licensee is exempt from which requirement that would otherwise apply?
choice_a: The duty to comply with fair housing laws
choice_b: The duty to hold trust funds in a separate account
choice_c: The duty to hold a real estate license
choice_d: The duty to present every written offer in a timely manner (§76-2417(1)(c)(ii)/§76-2418(1)(c)(ii)), and from including certain §76-2417 duties in the written agreement under §76-2422(2)
explanation: Section 76-2422.01 exempts licensees from the timely-offer-presentation duty and from including specified §76-2417 duties in the written agreement when the client is an asset management company.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2423(1)(a), a brokerage relationship commences at the time the licensee begins representing a client and continues until:
choice_a: Performance or completion of the representation
choice_b: The property closes, with no earlier termination possible
choice_c: The listing agreement is physically signed, regardless of when representation actually begins
choice_d: The commission issues a certificate of completion
explanation: Section 76-2423(1)(a) states the relationship commences when representation begins and continues until performance or completion of the representation.

question: Under §76-2423(2), even after a brokerage relationship terminates or expires, a licensee continues to owe which duties, absent a different written agreement?
choice_a: The full fiduciary duties of loyalty and good faith, indefinitely
choice_b: Accounting for all money and property related to and received during the relationship, and keeping confidential information confidential (subject to statutory exceptions)
choice_c: A continuing duty to seek additional offers on the client's behalf
choice_d: No duties whatsoever survive termination
explanation: Section 76-2423(2) survives termination only as to accounting for money/property and maintaining confidentiality, not the full package of representation duties.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2424(1), in a real estate transaction, a designated broker's compensation may be paid by:
choice_a: Only the party the broker represents
choice_b: Only the seller, regardless of which party the broker represents
choice_c: The seller, the landlord, the buyer, the tenant, a third party, or through sharing between designated brokers
choice_d: Only the State Real Estate Commission's fund
explanation: Section 76-2424(1) allows compensation to come from the seller, landlord, buyer, tenant, a third party, or via sharing between designated brokers.

question: Under §76-2424(2), the mere fact that a party pays a designated broker's compensation:
choice_a: Automatically creates an agency relationship with that paying party
choice_b: Automatically makes the broker a dual agent
choice_c: Voids any existing written agency agreement
choice_d: Does not by itself establish an agency relationship between that paying party and the designated broker or any affiliated licensee
explanation: Section 76-2424(2) clarifies that who pays compensation does not itself determine or create an agency relationship.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2425, a licensee's violation of any provision of sections 76-2401 to 76-2430 is treated as:
choice_a: An unfair trade practice under §81-885.24, subjecting the licensee to commission investigation and administrative action under the Nebraska Real Estate License Act
choice_b: A criminal felony prosecuted by the Attorney General
choice_c: A matter solely for private civil litigation, with no role for the commission
choice_d: Grounds for automatic revocation with no hearing rights
explanation: Section 76-2425 designates a violation of the agency-relationships sections as an unfair trade practice under §81-885.24, enforceable through commission investigation and administrative action.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2426(1), a client is liable for a misrepresentation made by his or her own limited agent arising out of the limited-agency agreement only if:
choice_a: The misrepresentation caused financial harm, regardless of the client's knowledge
choice_b: The client knew or should have known of the misrepresentation
choice_c: The client personally authorized the exact statement in writing
choice_d: A court finds the agent acted with malice
explanation: Section 76-2426(1) limits a client's liability for the agent's misrepresentation to situations where the client knew or should have known of it.

question: Under §76-2426(3)-(4), a limited agent is liable for a subagent's misrepresentation, and a subagent is liable for the primary limited agent's misrepresentation, only if:
choice_a: Any misrepresentation occurred anywhere in the transaction, regardless of knowledge
choice_b: The misrepresentation was made in writing
choice_c: The agent or subagent, as applicable, knew or should have known of the misrepresentation
choice_d: The commission had previously disciplined the other agent
explanation: Section 76-2426(3) and (4) each impose liability for another's misrepresentation only where the liable party knew or should have known of it.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2427, a designated broker who appoints specific affiliated licensees in writing to act as limited agents for a client, to the exclusion of other affiliated licensees:
choice_a: Automatically becomes a dual agent regardless of the appointment
choice_b: May never make such an appointment under Nebraska law
choice_c: Must obtain the commission's approval before making the appointment
choice_d: Is not considered a dual agent solely because of that appointment — though any individual licensee who personally represents both the seller and buyer (or landlord and tenant) in one transaction is a dual agent and must comply with §§76-2401 to 76-2430
explanation: Section 76-2427 allows appointment of designated limited agents without automatically creating dual agency for the broker, while still treating any individual who personally represents both sides of one transaction as a dual agent.

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-2429, sections 76-2401 to 76-2430:
choice_a: Supersede the duties and responsibilities of the parties under the common law, including the fiduciary responsibilities of an agent to a principal, except as provided in §76-2422(6)
choice_b: Merely supplement the common law of agency without changing it
choice_c: Apply only when the parties expressly opt into the common law
choice_d: Have been held unconstitutional and are not currently enforceable
explanation: Section 76-2429 makes the statutory limited-agent duties in §§76-2417 to 76-2419 supersede common-law fiduciary duties, except where the parties enter into a broader agreement under §76-2422(6), which remains subject to common-law agency principles.
